title: Do not build a portrait they did not state
summary: XiaoIce stores a user persona vector when it has a user id. Galion One forbids a portrait. HORBM stores statements the person asked to keep, and it does not infer age, gender, personality, diagnosis, or an emotion history.
body:
The XiaoIce preprint, opened, says that when a user id exists the empathy vector includes a user persona: gender, age, interests, occupation, personality, and similar profile fields. That is what their system did. It is not what this one does.

Galion One: do not collect a portrait of them for later. Do not store a story they did not ask to keep. Do not name their emotion back to them. Galion Research: do not collect the question into a profile, and do not keep a research notebook of their affect. `sense` is not a licence to "research them."

R3's opinion, adopted here, draws the line at statements rather than inferences. Allowed on disk, and only with `remember` granted for that write: a name or address form they asked to be used, a fact they asked to keep, and a correction of a previous kept fact. Each row keeps the source turn, who said it, the date, and the consent bits from that moment.

Refused, even if `remember` is on: inferred age, gender, personality, diagnosis, or an emotion history; a label such as "anxious person" or "night owl" derived from the voice; and a copy of the caller's affect baseline into the user table. The affect baseline, if it is kept at all, stays in the existing affect store's own remember path, which the lock ties to a consented store. HORBM does not duplicate it.

The Act's recital, opened, says emotion recognition can be intrusive and that expression varies across cultures and within a person. That is a reason not to freeze a fleeting frame into a trait. It is not, by itself, the product rule. The product rule is the persona file: no portrait.

Session-only state, in RAM, may include the language of this call and a want they stated this call. It dies at hang-up unless a specific write was granted. It is not a profile.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
sources.author: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.note: Official Journal L series, 12.7.2024. HTML opened 2026-11-18. Article 5(1)(f) prohibits AI systems that infer emotions in workplace and education institutions, with a medical or safety exception. Recital text in the same HTML says emotion recognition identifies or infers emotions from biometric data, and that expressions vary across cultures.
